$comment: The one place published names, the engine's Nx project and directory, the NAPI platform rows and the publish switches are declared. Workflows, scripts and tests read this file; rename here and nowhere else. A row's `container` is the pinned image its producer builds in (a Linux row builds in manylinux for its glibc floor); `floor` is an extra consumer cell that installs the candidate on the oldest supported distribution.

wasm.$comment: The WASM module and its part of the source and relink kit are built by their own producer job on this hosted runner, in parallel with the native producers. It must be a host of the selected delivery recipe's `wasmHost` (x86_64 Linux): the recipe pins that host's Emscripten SDK and nightly Rust.

geospec.$comment: The TypeScript DSL, runner and CLI (`npx geospec run`). It shares the engine's fixed release group, so a `geospec` version always names the `geospec-engine` version it depends on exactly.

ci.$comment: A platform row's `selfHosted` runner replaces its hosted `runner` (and every job on that hosted label) only for trusted events: a push or workflow_dispatch on main and, while `selfHostedPullRequests` is on, a pull request whose head is this repository and whose actor and author are not dependabot[bot]. Fork and Dependabot pull requests always stay on the hosted runner. `scripts/ci-plan.mjs` decides the route once per run. Off: the `local-mac-trusted` runner group (tau-cloud `stacks/repo/geospec`) admits only `ci.yml@refs/heads/main`, because a runner group cannot tell a same-repository pull request ref from a fork's.

publish.$comment: `geospecNpm` gates the `geospec` npm package on its own and stays off until npm trusts ci.yml + npm-publish in taucad/geospec for `geospec` (that package still trusts taucad/tau); setting it to true is the one change that starts publishing it beside the engine. npm is on: the trusted-publisher bindings for ci.yml + npm-publish exist (2026-10-13), so every main push publishes a next prerelease. PyPI is on for stable releases only: an exact release commit publishes its wheels after the release pull request passed qualification. A main push never publishes to PyPI; its wheels carry the PEP 440 .devN form of the next version and only pass the dry run's twine check.
